messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 incident — hosted-runtime-uswest kvcache OOMs detected (auto-escalation). Multiple hosts in pool showing rapid KV map growth and OOM spikes. Please ack and start triage. Incident ID: RWD-2026-312

alex_s: acked. seeing OOMs on 3 nodes in us-west-2 serving-hosted-2. symptoms: sustained client long prompts + continuous prefetch. spike started ~10:05 UTC.

mike_g: i'm oncall, taking it. pinging @tara_ops for customer comms and @sophia_r for handoff if we need longer coverage. quick question — any deploys in last hour?

eng-sre-bot: deploy-bot: no deploys to serving runtime in the last 2 hours.

alex_s: no recent runtime deploys. last config change was prefetch rollout 2 days ago (prefetch-depth=1024 for hosted tier to reduce cold latency). suspect prefetch depth amplification with long prompts.

mike_g: copying logs + quick grep for key metrics, past 15m:
```
# top 5 keys by kv_size growth
key_prefix_abc: 1.2G
session:9876: 900M
prompt:xxxx: 780M
user:2468: 420M
prefix:zz: 200M
```

mike_g: looks like a few large session prefixes are absorbing lots of KV. Continuous batching is keeping these alive across requests. memory per process > 90% then OOM.

alex_s: reproducer locally with long prompt 200k tokens causes same KV growth (weird but consistent with prefix amplification).

mike_g: mitigation plan (fast): 1) throttle prefetch depth to 64 (global) 2) reduce continuous batching max_batch_window to 50ms 3) enable kv-evict-on-critical to aggressively evict large prefixes temporarily 4) route heavy sessions to fallback small-context variant.

tara_ops: +1. I'll draft a status page note if we get errors hitting customers. any immediate impact counts?

mike_g: quick impact calc: 6% 503s on hosted runtime across us-west-2, affected customers: AcmeApp (primary), BetaCorp (sporadic). throughput degraded ~30% for those keys.

alex_s: i'm ready to apply config. command to patch config via infra control plane:
```
servicectl patch runtime-hosted-2 --set prefetch.depth=64 --set batching.max_window_ms=50 --set kvcache.evict_on_critical=true --comment "hotfix throttle prefetch after OOM surges"
```

mike_g: applying now. will monitor memory.

eng-sre-bot: rollout started: patch job ID rwd-hotfix-626789. targeting pool hosted-2 (20 nodes), rolling update 2 nodes at a time.

mike_g: nodes 1-4 patched, memory usage trending down on those:
```
node-01 mem%: 92 -> 68
node-02 mem%: 90 -> 65
node-03 mem%: 94 -> 67
```

mike_g: good signal. continuing rollout.

alex_s: adding temporary prefix bloom filter tweak to dedupe repeated prefixes for same session:
```
kvcache.prefix_dedupe=true
kvcache.dedupe_window_ms=30000
```

mike_g: dedupe change applied on canary nodes. observing KV map shrink on canary by ~40%.

tara_ops: customer impact update for status page draft:
- Users: impacted AcmeApp and BetaCorp (partial errors, 5-8% request error rate)
- Mitigation: throttled prefetch, reduced batching window, canary dedupe enabled; full rollout in progress
- ETA: monitoring, will update in 30m

sophia_r: taking next shift if this needs longer follow-up. handoff note: we applied prefetch cap -> immediate reduction in memory growth, but root cause likely prefetch policy + long prompt patterns causing persistent huge KV entries. need postmortem and prompt-length-based guardrails.

mike_g: rolling update completed across pool. mem utilization normalized across nodes (~60-70%). 503 rate dropped to baseline ~0.2%.

alex_s: confirming long tail keys still exist but are being evicted faster. starting data collection of top offending keys to repro owner mapping.

tara_ops: posted initial status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/RWD-2026-312 (placeholder). tagging support to reach out to AcmeApp SRE.

mike_g: initiated contact with AcmeApp on-call. they saw spikes between 10:04-10:18 UTC, accepted mitigation and will throttle on their side too.

eng-sre-bot: alert summary posted to incident channel, metrics snapshot attached.

alex_s: next steps: 1) create a bug for prefetch-depth default (issue #RWD-4502) 2) add server-side prompt-length guard that rejects/flags extreme requests > 50k tokens 3) add continuous-batching heuristics to lower persistence for long-session prefixes 4) run targeted eval to ensure latency impact acceptable.

mike_g: filing the ticket and assigning to @alex_s and @eng-infra.

mike_g: handoff to @sophia_r for postmortem and longer-term follow-up. I'm standing down but will be available if any regression.

sophia_r: acked. collecting timeline + logs, will schedule postmortem meeting.

tara_ops: thanks all — will finalize customer comms and update status page when PMs sign off.

mike_g: closing pager. leaving channel for async follow-ups. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident RWD-2026-312 marked resolved by mike_g at 10:46 UTC.

sophia_r: filing postmortem draft: summary, timeline, impact numbers, root cause hypothesis (prefetch depth x long prompts -> KV persistence), mitigations, action items (guardrails + canary checks). will ping for reviews.

alex_s: adding note to Optimize: consider automatic prefetch caps per-customer and priority-based prefetch budgets.

tara_ops: will coordinate customer follow-ups and share final comms. :pray:

mike_g: thanks team. great quick triage and rollback+hotfix sequencing.

sophia_r: assigning action items: [RWD-4502], [RWD-4503 prompt-guard], [RWD-4504 batch-heuristics]. expected owner + ETA in postmortem.

mike_g: handing off monitoring to eng-sre oncall with runbook link:
```
https://runbooks.redwood.ai/kvcache-oom-runbook
```

alex_s: +1 on runbook updates (include prefetch rollback steps and status page templates).

end of thread.
